syllabus:
The claim of letters-patent No. 187,100, granted to John Clark, February 6th, 1877, for an “improvement in cheese-formers for cider-presses,” namely, “The-guide-frame D, in combination with an extended pomace-rack, and a cloth to inclose a layer of pomace therein, substantially as described,” is invalid, because it did not require invention to use the described guide-frame in connection with the racks and the cloths.

.The racks and the cloths had been before used in connection, and' an enclosure was used with them, which enabled the operator to make the pom-ace of uniform depth on each rack, and prevented the lateral spreading of the pomace; and it required only ordinary mechanical skill and Judgment to make either the guide-frame or the rack of the desired size.

Mr. Justice Blatchford

delivered the opinion of the court.

This is a suit in equity brought in the Circuit Court of the United States for the Northern District of New York, for the infringement of letters-patent No. 187,100, -granted to John Clark, February 6th, 1877, for an “improvement in cheese-formers for cider-presses,” on an application filed September 11th, 1876.
